questions.question: Your new PivotTable's grand total is lower than =SUM of the Sales column. What is the most likely cause?

answerOptions.text: The pivot rounds every value to the nearest lakh
answerOptions.rationale: A pivot does not round values on its own.

answerOptions.text: Sales was placed in Rows instead of Values
answerOptions.rationale: Then there would be no Sum of Sales total to compare.

answerOptions.text: A blank row in the source data stopped the range, so rows below it were missed
answerOptions.rationale: Excel's automatic range stops at the first blank row.

answerOptions.text: The Branch filter is set to (All)
answerOptions.rationale: (All) includes every branch, so it would not lower the total.

questions.question: You want a rupee number format on Sum of Sales that survives refreshes and layout changes. What should you do?

answerOptions.text: Control-click a value > Number Format, and set the format for the field
answerOptions.rationale: Formatting the field, not the cells, keeps the format when the pivot changes.

answerOptions.text: Select the value cells and press Control Shift 1
answerOptions.rationale: Cell formatting is lost when the field is removed and added again.

answerOptions.text: Use Format Painter from a formatted cell
answerOptions.rationale: That is still cell formatting and can be lost on changes.

answerOptions.text: Untick Autofit column widths on update
answerOptions.rationale: That keeps column widths, not number formats.

questions.question: Months are in Rows and Sum of Sales in Values. How do you show how much sales rose or fell compared with the previous month?

answerOptions.text: Summarize Values By > Max
answerOptions.rationale: Max shows the largest invoice, not the change.

answerOptions.text: Show Values As > Running Total In, base field Region
answerOptions.rationale: Region is not in the pivot, so this gives #N/A, and it is a running total anyway.

answerOptions.text: Show Values As > % of Grand Total
answerOptions.rationale: That shows each month's share of the year, not the change.

answerOptions.text: Show Values As > Difference From, base field Month, base item (previous)
answerOptions.rationale: This shows each month's change from the month before.

questions.question: Grouping the Date field by Quarters gives Qtr1 = January to March. How do you report by the Indian April to March year?

answerOptions.text: Group by Months only and add them up by hand
answerOptions.rationale: That defeats the point of the pivot and is easy to get wrong.

answerOptions.text: Add FY and FY Qtr helper columns to the source data and use them in the pivot
answerOptions.rationale: Built-in date grouping follows the calendar year, so helper columns give the April to March split.

answerOptions.text: Set the Mac's region to India
answerOptions.rationale: The region setting does not change how pivot quarters are grouped.

answerOptions.text: Move Date to the Values area
answerOptions.rationale: A field in Values cannot be grouped at all.

questions.question: You need margin % by category that is correct at every level, including the grand total. What is the best method?

answerOptions.text: A Calculated Field: =(Sales-Cost)/Sales
answerOptions.rationale: It works on the totals of each row, so the ratio is right at every level.

answerOptions.text: Add the Line Margin % column from the source and sum it
answerOptions.rationale: Summing percentages gives meaningless numbers in the thousands of percent.

answerOptions.text: Add the Line Margin % column and set it to Average
answerOptions.rationale: A simple average treats a small order the same as a big deal.

answerOptions.text: A Calculated Item that adds two categories
answerOptions.rationale: Calculated items add new items and can double-count in the grand total.

questions.question: Two pivots come from the same data. You click South on a Region slicer, but only one pivot changes. What is the fix?

answerOptions.text: Rename the slicer caption in Slicer Settings
answerOptions.rationale: The caption is only a label; it does not link pivots.

answerOptions.text: Click Refresh All on the Data tab
answerOptions.rationale: Refresh re-reads data; it does not connect a slicer.

answerOptions.text: Use Command-click on South
answerOptions.rationale: Command-click selects several slicer items; it does not add connections.

answerOptions.text: Select the slicer, then Slicer tab > Report Connections, and tick the second pivot
answerOptions.rationale: A new slicer filters only its own pivot until you connect others.

questions.question: Which of these chart types will Excel refuse to use for a PivotChart?

answerOptions.text: Line
answerOptions.rationale: Line is allowed and is the usual choice for monthly trends.

answerOptions.text: Treemap
answerOptions.rationale: Treemap, sunburst, scatter, histogram, waterfall and map are not allowed for PivotCharts.

answerOptions.text: Clustered column
answerOptions.rationale: Column charts are allowed for PivotCharts.

answerOptions.text: Pie
answerOptions.rationale: Pie is one of the allowed PivotChart types.

questions.question: You paste March invoices below the existing data and click Refresh, but the pivot does not change. Why?

answerOptions.text: Pivots can only be refreshed once a day
answerOptions.rationale: There is no such limit.

answerOptions.text: You must close and reopen the workbook first
answerOptions.rationale: Reopening does not change the pivot's source range.

answerOptions.text: Refresh only re-reads the original range; use Change Data Source or build the pivot on a Table
answerOptions.rationale: New rows outside the source range are ignored until the range grows.

answerOptions.text: GETPIVOTDATA is blocking the refresh
answerOptions.rationale: GETPIVOTDATA only reads from the pivot; it does not stop a refresh.
